bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI focused on systems that learn from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns from data to make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Crucial in modern tech, used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Supervised Learning: Trained on labeled data to predict known outputs.
Supervised Learning includes Regression (continuous output) and Classification (categorical output).
Unsupervised Learning: Trained on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns or structures.
Unsupervised Learning includes Clustering (grouping data) and Dimensionality Reduction (reducing features).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize rewards.
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust parameters.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split to train the model and evaluate its performance on unseen data.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor generalization.
Underfitting: Model is too simple and fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationship for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicts probability of belonging to a class.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data into subsets for decision-making.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns for deep learning applications.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Evaluate model performance using separate datasets.
Metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score for classification; MSE, R-squared for regression.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data by splitting into subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Adjusting model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance using methods like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: Models need large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: Complex models, especially deep learning, are hard to understand.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues where models either learn noise or are too simplistic.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will lead to more powerful and transparent systems.
ML applications will integrate more into daily life across various industries.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be crucial as the field progresses.
